Unicode versus visible letters

A precomposed letter such as Ḃ is one code point. A letter plus an uncomposed mark may be two code points but appear as one grapheme. NFC combines them only when Unicode defines an equivalent character.

How to use the keyboard

1 · Touch or mouse

Tap for a normal letter. Hold a key until its menu appears, then tap a variation or slide onto one and release. Use ⇧ for capitals and ?123 for more symbols.

2 · Physical keyboard

Enable physical-keyboard hold above. In the writing area, hold a letter or punctuation key to open options. Choose with mouse/touch or arrow keys and Enter. Ordinary quick taps type normally.

3 · Extra Unicode

While holding a letter, switch to Combining marks for all 112 original marks. The full 368-character reference, custom keys, favorites, import/export, and NFC controls remain available.

Optional private profile sync

Save keyboard appearance and layout preferences to your existing Savanski v1 backend. No pairing or account required; each browser gets its own anonymous profile.

Cloud sync is optional. Typed text, clipboard contents, and keystrokes are never sent.

Includes the original U+1E00–U+1EFF and U+0300–U+036F collection, plus accent and symbol alternatives. Works as a browser/PWA writing keyboard, not as a system-wide keyboard for unrelated apps. Rendering of rare symbols depends on installed device fonts. Unicode character names are bundled in local JSON and available offline after installation. Unicode Consortium

Design & sizing

Choose a part from the menu or press “Pick on keyboard,” then tap the part you want to recolor. The color wheel applies only to that selected part.

Changes are stored only on this device. Typed text is not sent to a server. OS-level keyboard injection, screenshots, and secure-field access require a native app.
